HMLR_S6_UPDATED_20150625
Practice Guide 41 supplement 6 was updated on 25 June 2015.
HMLR_S6_APPLIES_EW
The overriding-interests supplement applies to England and Wales.
HMLR_S6_OGL3
The supplement is licensed under the Open Government Licence version 3.0 except where otherwise stated.
HMLR_S6_SECTION71_DUTY
Section 71 of the Land Registration Act 2002 creates a duty to disclose certain overriding interests.
HMLR_S6_RULE57_DUTY
Rule 57 of the Land Registration Rules 2003 also governs disclosure of certain overriding interests.
HMLR_S6_REGISTRABLE_DISPOSITION
The disclosure duty applies when registering a registrable disposition of a registered estate.
HMLR_S6_TRANSFER_TRIGGER
A transfer application is one of the transactions that can trigger the disclosure duty.
HMLR_S6_LEASE_TRIGGER
A lease application is one of the transactions that can trigger the disclosure duty.
HMLR_S6_CHARGE_TRIGGER
A charge application is one of the transactions that can trigger the disclosure duty.
HMLR_S6_EASEMENT_TRIGGER
A grant of easement can trigger the disclosure duty.
HMLR_S6_MULTIPLOT_ADVANTAGE
Noting an interest before development can benefit parties where the interest affects more than one plot.
HMLR_S6_DEVELOPER_NO_REPEAT_DISCLOSURE
Once an interest is noted, the developer need not reveal it repeatedly as an overriding interest to each purchaser.
HMLR_S6_DEVELOPER_LESS_DOCUMENTATION
Prior notation can reduce the supporting documentation supplied to each purchaser.
HMLR_S6_DEVELOPER_LESS_CORRESPONDENCE
Prior notation can reduce correspondence between the developer and HM Land Registry.
HMLR_S6_PURCHASER_EARLY_VISIBILITY
Purchasers can see most relevant interests on the register before committing to buy.
HMLR_S6_LESSEE_EARLY_VISIBILITY
Lessees can see most relevant interests on the register before committing.
HMLR_S6_FEWER_UNREGISTERED_OVERRIDING
Prior notation reduces the number of unregistered overriding interests purchasers must investigate.
HMLR_S6_HMLR_SINGLE_REVIEW
HM Land Registry can consider a noted interest once rather than on every plot application.
HMLR_S6_AN1
The voluntary application is made using form AN1.
HMLR_S6_SUPPORTING_DOCUMENTS
Form AN1 should be accompanied by supporting documentation.
HMLR_S6_DI_OPTION
Form DI may be used to help set out relevant evidence and details.
HMLR_S6_ONE_AN1
Only one AN1 application is needed regardless of the number of overriding interests being noted.
HMLR_S6_RESTRICTION_CONTACT
A developer should contact the Developer Team before applying if a restriction prevents noting.
HMLR_S6_CAUTION_CONTACT
A developer should contact the Developer Team before applying if a caution against dealings exists.
HMLR_S6_NOTICE_ON_REGISTER
When satisfied with the evidence, HM Land Registry will usually enter a notice on the register.
HMLR_PG72_UPDATED_20191125
Practice Guide 72 was updated on 25 November 2019.
HMLR_PG72_APPLIES_EW
The development-schemes guide applies to England and Wales.
HMLR_PG72_OGL3
Practice Guide 72 is licensed under the Open Government Licence version 3.0 except where otherwise stated.
HMLR_PG72_PIECEMEAL_ACQUISITION
A development scheme supports acquisition of a specified area in separate parcels over time.
HMLR_PG72_SINGLE_TITLE
The procedure can incorporate acquired parcels progressively into one registered title.
HMLR_PG72_PUBLIC_AUTHORITY
A local or other public authority may request a development scheme.
HMLR_PG72_COMPANY
A company may request a development scheme.
HMLR_PG72_CORPORATE_BODY
Another corporate body may request a development scheme.
HMLR_PG72_REDEVELOPMENT_EXAMPLE
A redevelopment programme is an example use case for a development scheme.
HMLR_PG72_REPLACES_SCHEME_TITLES
Development schemes have replaced the older scheme-title procedure.
HMLR_PG72_EXISTING_SCHEME_CONTINUE
Existing active scheme titles continue under arrangements already agreed with the developer.
HMLR_PG72_COMPULSORY_OR_VOLUNTARY
The procedure can be used whether land is acquired compulsorily or voluntarily.
HMLR_PG72_PROGRESSIVE_BUILDUP
The procedure allows the registered title to build up progressively.
HMLR_PG72_AVOIDS_MANY_TITLES
The procedure avoids numerous separate titles that would later require amalgamation.
HMLR_PG72_NOMINATED_STAFF
Nominated HM Land Registry staff oversee applications throughout the scheme.
HMLR_PG72_PRECOMMENCE_DISCUSSION
Known extent or title-evidence problems can be discussed before the scheme starts.
HMLR_PG72_PROCESS_ARRANGEMENTS
Detailed arrangements can be agreed for preparing, lodging and processing applications.
HMLR_PG72_LIAISON_UNEXPECTED
HM Land Registry liaises with the applicant to resolve unexpected issues while the scheme runs.
HMLR_PG72_SUPPLY_ALL_FACTS
The applicant must provide all relevant facts before suitability can be decided.
HMLR_PG72_EARLY_CONTACT
The applicant should contact HM Land Registry as early as possible.
HMLR_PG72_TOTAL_AREA_PLAN
Initial contact should include a plan identifying the total acquisition area.
HMLR_PG72_CPO_COPY
A relevant compulsory purchase order should be supplied where applicable.
HMLR_PG72_EXPLAIN_DEVELOPMENT
The initial letter should explain the development planned for the area.
HMLR_PG72_ACQUISITION_PROGRAMME
The initial letter should describe the programme for acquiring properties.
HMLR_PG72_DISPOSAL_PROGRAMME
Where appropriate, the initial letter should describe the programme for disposing of new properties.
HMLR_PG72_INTERESTS_TO_ACQUIRE
The initial letter should identify the interests in land that must be acquired.
HMLR_PG72_LEASEHOLD_EXAMPLE
Leasehold interests are an example of interests that should be identified.
HMLR_PG72_RENTCHARGE_EXAMPLE
Rentcharges are an example of interests that should be identified.
HMLR_PG72_OWNERSHIP_DIFFICULTY
Areas where ownership may be difficult to establish should be identified.
HMLR_PG72_REASONABLE_TIME
Successful operation depends on intending to acquire properties within a reasonable time.
HMLR_PG72_REGISTERED_OR_UNREGISTERED
Land in a scheme may be registered, unregistered or a mixture of both.
HMLR_PG72_SEPARATE_LEASEHOLD
Leasehold interests are registered separately within the development scheme.
HMLR_PG72_SEPARATE_RENTCHARGE
Rentcharges are registered separately within the development scheme.
HMLR_PG72_CAREFUL_EARLY_PLANNING
Careful planning in the first stages is important to the procedure.
HMLR_PG72_MEETING_NORMAL
HM Land Registry will normally request a meeting after receiving the basic information.
HMLR_PG72_CLOSE_LIAISON
Close liaison is required if the scheme proceeds.
HMLR_PG72_REPORT_PROBLEMS
The applicant must report problems immediately.
HMLR_PG72_REPORT_PLAN_CHANGES
The applicant must report changes in development plans immediately.
HMLR_PG72_LARGE_SCALE_PLANS
Final arrangements require one or more large-scale plans.
HMLR_PG72_LATEST_OS_BASE
Scheme plans must be based on the latest edition of the Ordnance Survey map.
HMLR_PG72_URBAN_1250
The normal urban plan scale is 1:1250.
HMLR_PG72_RURAL_2500
The normal rural plan scale is 1:2500.
HMLR_PG72_COLOURED_EDGING
Scheme plans should use coloured edging to show land intended for acquisition.
HMLR_PG72_PG40_COMPLIANCE
Scheme plans must meet HM Land Registry land-identification requirements in Practice Guide 40.
HMLR_PG72_ELECTRONIC_IMPORT
Compatible mapping data may be imported electronically by arrangement.
HMLR_PG72_REFERENCE_NUMBER
HM Land Registry supplies a reference number for scheme applications and correspondence.
HMLR_PG72_QUOTE_REFERENCE
The scheme reference must be quoted in related applications, enquiries and correspondence.
